key_insight: An interpretable 13-feature model mined from discharge reports can predict atrial fibrillation risk in cardiovascular patients better than common clinical risk scores.
clinical_relevance: This could help hospitals flag higher-risk patients during routine follow-up using data already present in electronic health records.
method: Single-center retrospective study of 17,562 cardiovascular patients without prior AF.
Custom NLP converted discharge reports into 73 structured features; models were built with LightAutoML.
Developed a full model, a simpler 13-feature model (Pre-AF 13), and a linear bedside score (Pre-AF 9).
evidence_signal: In 80,576 records from 45,000 patients, the best model achieved ROC AUC 0.735 for 24-month AF prediction and 0.696 over full follow-up, outperforming CHARGE-AF, C2HEST, MHS, and HAVOC.
watch_item: This was a single-center retrospective study, so performance may not generalize without external validation and prospective testing.
paper_title: Pre-AF 13: An Interpretable Atrial Fibrillation Risk Score Mined from Discharge Reports
